fields.title: Live modelling: adviser builds a payment-reminder prompt thinking aloud
fields.contentOrLocator:
The adviser opens a blank LLM chat and types: 'Write a payment reminder.' The output is polite but has no customer, amount, or deadline. The adviser says: 'That is too vague. A real customer would ignore it.' Next the adviser types: 'You are a small business owner. Write a payment reminder to a fictional customer for an unpaid invoice.' The output names a business context but still invents or omits the customer name and amount. The adviser says: 'Better, but it still lacks specifics.' Then the adviser adds: 'Be firm and demand payment immediately.' The output becomes aggressive and threatens legal action. The adviser says: 'This made it worse. A stronger tone is not always better.' Finally the adviser types: 'You are the owner of a fictional design studio. Write a polite payment reminder to a fictional customer named Samira Patel for invoice INV-2024-047 (£185 for website maintenance), issued 14 days ago. Ask for payment within 7 days. Offer to discuss if there is a problem. Keep it under 100 words.' The output names a fictional customer, gives an invoice reference and amount, sets a deadline, and stays polite. The adviser says: 'Those are prompt moves: role, recipient, details, tone, and constraint. I used only fictional details—no real customer names or real invoices.'

## Thinking aloud: building a first payment-reminder prompt

Adviser: I need a payment reminder for a fictional customer. Let me start with what feels natural: 'Write a payment reminder.' That is all I give the model. Here is what comes back. [Shows output.] It is polite, but it does not say who owes what, or by when. A real customer would ignore it. So the first prompt move I can see is: the prompt is too vague. It lacks role, recipient, and specifics. Adviser: Let me add a role and a task: 'You are a small business owner. Write a payment reminder to a fictional customer for an unpaid invoice.' [Shows output.] Better. It knows it is a business context. But it still invents the customer name and amount, or leaves them blank. It does not know the invoice is £185 or that it is two weeks overdue. Adviser: Now I want to test whether tone words change the result. I will add: 'Be firm and demand payment immediately.' [Shows output.] This made it worse. The model sounds aggressive and threatens legal action. For a first message to a long-standing customer, that could damage the relationship. So tone is a prompt move, and a stronger tone is not always better. Adviser: Let me revise: 'You are the owner of a fictional design studio. Write a polite payment reminder to a fictional customer named Samira Patel for invoice INV-2024-047 (£185 for website maintenance), issued 14 days ago. Ask for payment within 7 days. Offer to discuss if there is a problem. Keep it under 100 words.' [Shows output.] This version names a fictional customer, gives an invoice reference and amount, sets a clear deadline, and keeps the tone polite. Those are prompt moves: role, recipient, details, tone, and constraint. Notice I used only fictional details—no real customer names or real invoices. Adviser: Your turn. Pick one routine message from your own business and try it.

## Weak, worse, and improved payment-reminder prompts

Weak prompt: 'Write a payment reminder.' Worse prompt (one change that made output worse): 'You are a small business owner. Write a payment reminder to a fictional customer for an unpaid invoice. Be firm and demand payment immediately.' Improved prompt: 'You are the owner of a fictional design studio. Write a polite payment reminder to a fictional customer named Samira Patel for invoice INV-2024-047 (£185 for website maintenance), issued 14 days ago. Ask for payment within 7 days. Offer to discuss if there is a problem. Keep it under 100 words.'

fields.title: Peer owner shows her own prompts, failures included
fields.contentOrLocator:
Peer owner Maya runs a fictional bakery called 'Rose & Crumb' in the fictional town of Brackley. First prompt (failed): 'Post on Facebook about our cakes.' The output was generic, with no location, no offer, and no call to action. Second prompt (revised): 'Write a Facebook post for a fictional bakery called Rose & Crumb in fictional town Brackley. Announce a fictional weekend sourdough workshop on Saturday 14 June at 10am. Mention that places are limited to 8. Keep it friendly and under 90 words. Include a fictional booking email bookings@roseandcrumb.example.' Maya says: 'The first one was too vague, so nobody knew where we were or how to book. The second one gave the model a place, a date, a limit, and a tone.'

## Peer owner prompts: failed and revised

Peer owner: Maya, fictional bakery 'Rose & Crumb', fictional town Brackley. Failed prompt: 'Post on Facebook about our cakes.' Revised prompt: 'Write a Facebook post for a fictional bakery called Rose & Crumb in fictional town Brackley. Announce a fictional weekend sourdough workshop on Saturday 14 June at 10am. Mention that places are limited to 8. Keep it friendly and under 90 words. Include a fictional booking email bookings@roseandcrumb.example.' Maya's comment: 'The first one was too vague, so nobody knew where we were or how to book. The second one gave the model a place, a date, a limit, and a tone.'

fields.title: Tick prompt moves on a card while watching
fields.contentOrLocator:
Prompt moves card (tick box version): [ ] Role — who is speaking (for example, small business owner). [ ] Recipient — who the message is for (for example, fictional customer Samira Patel). [ ] Task — what the message should do (for example, request payment). [ ] Details — names, amounts, invoice references, dates (for example, invoice INV-2024-047, £185). [ ] Tone — polite, firm, friendly (for example, polite but clear). [ ] Constraints — word count, deadline, format (for example, under 100 words, pay within 7 days). [ ] Call to action — what the customer should do next (for example, pay within 7 days or contact us if there is a problem).

## Prompt moves observation card

Prompt moves card — tick each move you observe while watching the adviser and the peer owner. You may tick a move more than once. [ ] Role — who is speaking. [ ] Recipient — who the message is for. [ ] Task — what the message should do. [ ] Details — names, amounts, invoice references, dates. [ ] Tone — polite, firm, friendly. [ ] Constraints — word count, deadline, format. [ ] Call to action — what the customer should do next. Notes: ...

fields.title: Write a first prompt for your own business and explain two choices
fields.contentOrLocator:
Write-your-own-prompt worksheet: Step 1 — Choose your message type (payment reminder or social media post). Step 2 — Write your prompt below using only fictional names, invoice references, and amounts. Step 3 — Explain Choice 1: what you chose and why. Step 4 — Explain Choice 2: what you chose and why. Step 5 — Check: did I use any real customer names or real invoice data? If yes, replace them with fictional details.

## Write your first business prompt

Step 1: Choose one routine customer message from your own business (payment reminder or social media post). Step 2: Write a prompt for an LLM below. Use only fictional customer details — no real names, real invoice numbers, or real personal data. My prompt: ________________________________________________________ Step 3: Explain Choice 1. What did you choose in your prompt, and what effect did you expect? ________________________________________________________ Step 4: Explain Choice 2. What did you choose in your prompt, and what effect did you expect? ________________________________________________________ Step 5: Check. Did you use any real customer names or real invoice data? If yes, replace them with fictional details before finishing.

## Weak, worse, and improved payment-reminder prompts

Weak prompt: 'Write a payment reminder.' Worse prompt (one change that made output worse): 'You are a small business owner. Write a payment reminder to a fictional customer for an unpaid invoice. Be firm and demand payment immediately.' Improved prompt: 'You are the owner of a fictional design studio. Write a polite payment reminder to a fictional customer named Samira Patel for invoice INV-2024-047 (£185 for website maintenance), issued 14 days ago. Ask for payment within 7 days. criteria.description: The prompt includes recipient, task, and business-specific details appropriate to a routine customer message.

levels.descriptor: The prompt contains no recipient, task, or business detail; it is a single vague phrase such as 'Write a reminder.'
The prompt includes either a recipient or a task, but not both, and lacks business-specific details such as invoice amount or due date.
The prompt includes a recipient, a task, and at least two business-specific details, for example fictional customer name, invoice reference, amount, or overdue period.
The prompt includes a recipient, a task, business-specific details, and an explicit tone or length constraint appropriate to a customer message.

criteria.description: The learner explains two prompt choices and links each to an expected effect on the output.

levels.descriptor: The learner gives no explanation or says 'I just wrote it.'
The learner identifies one choice, for example 'I added a name,' but does not say why.
The learner explains two choices and links each to an effect on the output, for example 'I added the invoice amount so the customer knows what is owed.'
The learner explains two choices, links each to an effect, and identifies one change they tried that made the output worse and why.

criteria.description: The prompt uses entirely fictional customer details and no real personal data.

levels.descriptor: The prompt uses real customer names, real invoice numbers, or real personal data.
The prompt mixes fictional names with real-looking invoice formats, amounts, or contact details.
The prompt uses entirely fictional customer names, invoice references, and amounts throughout, with no real personal data.
